title: Model intake playbook: SLA tiers, novelty scoring, and version pinning flow
creator: Asha Rao
description:
Purpose: provide an actionable, repeatable playbook for triaging model catalog requests from customers and internal teams, with explicit SLA tiers, a numeric novelty/fit scoring rubric, and a deterministic version-pinning + deprecation flow for enterprise tenants. Scope: new model adds (open-source and third-party), model version pinning requests, planned deprecations, and the eval-gate sequence for enterprise workloads. Out of scope: model training, model architecture research, and infra-only performance tuning requests (handled by ENG backlog).

Goals: 1) Reduce time-to-decision for intake requests to <= 5 business days for P0/P1 enterprise asks, 2) Ensure consistent risk & license assessment before a model is published to prod, 3) Make version pinning predictable (contractual pin windows) and deprecation predictable (>= 90 days notice for pinned versions), 4) Provide a clear eval gate checklist for enterprise security/compliance teams.

Intake form (minimum fields): requestor, customer tier (self-serve | paid | enterprise), requested model (name + provenance URL), model license, primary use case, latency & throughput expectations, dataset provenance notes, PII/Risk flags, requested SLA / pin window, urgency justification, and attachments (sample prompts/expected outputs).

Triage matrix and novelty scoring (numeric): - Business impact (0-5): customer ROI / feature criticality - Compatibility (0-5): architecture matches runtime (quantized-ready, supported ops) - Risk (0-5, inverted): licensing concerns, toxicity, hallucination risk - Operational cost (0-5): expected tokens/latency/cost delta - Security/compliance (0-5, inverted): data residency, model provenance concerns - Innovation bonus (0-2): proprietary features or clear accuracy gains
Total novelty_score = sum (0-27). Routing: >=20 -> fast-track (PM + Eng review within 48h), 14-19 -> standard review (5 business days), <=13 -> low-priority/batched review.

SLA tiers (response time = decision on whether to proceed to onboarding eval): - Tier S0 (enterprise paid SLA add-on): 48 business hours
- Tier S1 (high-revenue enterprise): 5 business days
- Tier S2 (self-serve paid or low-touch): 10 business days
- Tier S3 (community / research requests): batched monthly review
SLA is measured from intake submission to formal disposition (accept | accept-with-conditions | reject | request-more-info).

Eval gates (sequence for accepted requests): 1) Smoke test (automated run on representative prompts, latency profile, token cost estimate) 2) Safety pass (toxicity & prompt-injection checks, offense scoring) 3) Licensing & provenance verification (legal signoff if non-OSI or proprietary restrictions) 4) Quantization + compatibility tests (small-run on target infra) 5) Enterprise compliance checks (data residency, KMS integration, FIPS/HSM requirements) 6) Performance SLO validation (p99 latency under expected concurrency) 7) Regression monitoring plan (baseline prompt set + metric thresholds)
Acceptance criteria: pass steps 1-4 with documented artifacts and signoffs; steps 5-7 gated for enterprise customers or if model will be served under dedicated/private deployments.

Version pinning policy: - Default: no pin (customers use latest stable unless requested). - Enterprise pin request must specify pin window (3/6/12 months) and justification. - Pin request triggers an automated risk & compatibility review; PM decision within SLA. - If a security patch / critical bug occurs to the model family, Redwood reserves right to propose emergency changes; enterprise customers will be offered fallback model or expedited backport. - Deprecation windows: 90 days notice for non-pinned models; for pinned models, provide at least 90-day notice before pinned-end-of-life and a migration plan.

Deprecation flow: 1) Deprecation proposal published (owner + reason) 2) Impact analysis (list of pinned customers, ingestion of telemetry) 3) Customer outreach (email + Console banner + dedicated migration support for enterprise) 4) Migration plan & tooling (compatibility shim, prompt diffing doc) 5) End-of-life date + last-day-for-requests.

Metrics to track: intake-to-decision time, time in each eval gate, percent of requests rejected due to license/security, number of emergency deprecations, average novelty_score by outcome, enterprise satisfaction for onboarding.

Risks & mitigations: - Legal risk (license conflicts): require legal review before prod publish; short-circuit by rejecting non-compatible licenses. - Capacity risk (spike in requests): enforce SLA tiers and queueing; offer paid accelerated onboarding. - Regressions in quality: require regression test set + automated monitoring pre/post rollout.

Rollout plan: 1) Pilot with three enterprise customers and internal platform teams (Q2 2026), 2) Iterate playbook + intake form based on pilot feedback (4-week sprint), 3) Launch as default intake flow on Console with a small accelerator badge for paid SLAs, 4) Measure and refine.

Decision owners: PM (product-management) owns intake rubric and prioritization; Eng owners (serving runtime) own compatibility verification; Security/Legal required signoff on licensing and compliance checks.

Deliverables: intake form templates, triage rubric sheet (spreadsheet), Confluence playbook, automation in Console for routing & SLA tracking, guardrail check scripts in ENG repo.
